Potion Craft has one of those mechanics that immediately feels different from almost anything else in the genre.
Instead of simply selecting ingredients from a recipe, you physically navigate around an alchemy map. Different ingredients, grinding levels, paths, bases, and combinations give you different ways of reaching the same effect, which creates a surprising amount of freedom despite how simple the basic system looks.
The shopkeeping side is much more straightforward, and overall I would say the game is fairly easy. Once you understand the mechanics and start accumulating money, the difficulty drops dramatically.
Visually, though, the game has a lot of personality. The manuscript-style artwork is distinctive, and the music and sound design make it an extremely relaxing game to play.
My biggest issue appeared after many hours: repetition.

100% completion. This game is incredibly creative. It maps the linear progression of potion recipes onto a 2D adventure map, turning the potions themselves into the main characters explore and challenge through the map. Exploring and discovering each recipe feels like going on a grand adventure, and there are seemingly tons of possibilities to flip, twist, and maneuver the way around. And I absolutely love the art style. Every game asset and animation is wonderfully designed and full of personality.

The late game gets way too grindy. I was constantly repeating all the work did earlier, over and over again. Even though I have already unlocked all the potion recipes, I was practically wearing out my hand clicking through everything, even with a trainer. And all these bizarre customers, every single one of them talks in riddles. So damn annoying.

But anyway, I love the game has continued

This was a fun little puzzle/business simulator game! There is a whole community of players and a fandom page with guides if you choose to use them. Making potions in water is straightforward, but once you get to oil and wine, different mechanics come into play that add new layers of complexity to the challenge. I really enjoyed the dialogue between the customers, especially the shady ones. Sometimes it would be straightforward like, "I want to curse my neighbor..." and other times they will go through this entire diatribe to tell you that they need a poison.
The Key skills required to master this game:
1. Reading between the lines- As mentioned above, not all of the customers are straightforward with what they need.
2. Spatial perception- every ingredient creates a trail, and the goal is to finesse them towards a desired effect(s).

Potion cooking is made in a way where you explore through different maps and find new effects, which you end up selling. There's a bit of farming in the game (buy seed, plant,water,harvest, repeat). There's a couple unique customers you start getting at a certain point in the game. You also get to decorate your spaces. Using the alchemy engine can be fun. However making salts nearing chapter ten gets tedious due to the recipes requiring five different effects scattered all over the map. Yet this is necessary for you to progress further. That is the only part of the game I do not enjoy. 
Overall cozy, calm, turns my mind off. 
9/10

A splendidly fun simulation game requiring just the right amount of thinking. It strikes a perfect balance between relaxing and making you to think. Definitely worth getting during a Steam sale.
By the time this review is written, I have only completed the game on Normal mode. The following review might be irrelevant if you are playing on other difficulty levels. Early game is just about exploring the water map. You will learn to use different materials as you traverse the map searching for the right effects to add into your potion (or mushroom soup XD). Money can be earned by selling the potions you brew, and with sufficient money you can unlock salt and crystal recipes. Things get interesting when you start transmuting potions into different crystals and salts. The rule of thumb here is to make sure every chamber matches the one shown in the recipe before heating. TLDR; progression is terrible, this game disguises inconvenience with "challenging gameplay" 

There seems to be a lot of content for a few days whether that's encountering merchants, wizards (?) or unique descriptive customers that wants a potion for maybe legal reasons. Making a potion is straight-forward, dump the ingredients on the cauldron and apart from gameplay, the art style is nice. Depending on your preference of "cozy", this does have repetitive gameplay but most aspects don't necessarily have a tutorial so they're challenging in a way that you have to figure a lot of things out. 

Finding potion recipes is quite annoying. The way to go about it is fairly simple, but because you use your own potion ingredients to find recipes that aren't guaranteed, it comes off as inconvenient rather than challenging. The price difference with selling and buying potions/ingredients is crazy.
Pretty disappointed with the game play. After a few times, the potion making is just tedious and not really fun anymore. Wish to have a more dynamic play.

Substandard tutorial. Boring game loop. Visual cues as to when you're done grinding something (waste of players' time) are insufficient; bug and/or said bad visuals means I literally had to restart the tutorial, which is never a good sign. And wait, the tutorial doesn't even explain everything, you need to click into a submenu to get details on that. Some might call the aesthetic consistent and pleasing, but instead everything looks samey and it's hard to tell what's a button and what's not. The skill tree has exciting and earth-shaking upgrades like... sell a potion for 5% more. Haggle better. Harvest more stuff. Snooze... Oh but don't worry you can rearrange the furniture in your store. Truly compelling.

I had been there from the beginning. Many updates have been done, and I've sunk many hours into the game. And where it stands, I still cannot recommend it. Especially since the end-game mechanics are still non-existent, plus some updates worsened things:

1) The watering mechanic adds literally NOTHING to the game but stretch gameplay hours out and increase the grind.
2) There is no reward for the grind. I've unlocked every talend and skill in the tree, but the game still sits at two gardens, one crystal cave, and one mushroom cave. All additional items are solely decorative.
3) Talking about the garden, fertilization is only possible once per day. No way to grind for seeds there with that talent, making you wait days and days to have one of the merchants provide more seeds for plants or crystals you actually need.

Changing recipes for the alchemy machine with an update is fine, I guess
